title: Push-out test: what the MPa measures
topic: How a push-out test turns peak force into MPa, and why that number is a lab-specific dislodgement stress, not a clinical bond.

claims.claim: 1 mm slice of filled root (dentin, sealer, GP core)
claims.source: Pane ES et al., J Endod 2013;39(5):669-73 (PMID 23611388); Sagsen B et al., Int Endod J 2011;44(12):1088-91 (PMID 21895700)

claims.claim: Push apical → coronal (toward wider end), plunger Ø < canal Ø
claims.source: Deniz Sungur D et al., Restor Dent Endod 2016;41(2):114-20 (PMID 27200279); Pane ES et al., J Endod 2013;39(5):669-73 (PMID 23611388); Chen WP et al., J Endod 2013;39(2):283-7 (PMID 23321247)
Al-Haddad AY et al., Int J Biomater 2018:1731857 (PMID 30154852); load velocity affects MPa: Collares FM et al., Int Endod J 2016;49(9):836-49 (PMID 26331627)

claims.claim: Force climbs, then drops at debond; failure load = peak (F max 8.03 N)
claims.source: Failure load at the sudden drop: Al-Haddad AY et al., Int J Biomater 2018:1731857 (PMID 30154852). Curve shape and 8.03 N: Toy model / schematic, labelled 'toy model · values illustrative'

claims.claim: Failure modes: adhesive (sealer–dentin or sealer–GP), cohesive (within sealer, core or dentin), mixed; this specimen mixed
claims.source: Al-Haddad AY et al., Int J Biomater 2018:1731857 (PMID 30154852); Gesi A et al., J Endod 2005;31(11):809-13 (PMID 16249724); Ungor M et al., Int Endod J 2006;39(8):643-7 (PMID 16872459). Tiles are schematic

claims.claim: τ = F / A, A = canal-wall (frustum) area π(R+r)√((R−r)²+h²), nominal
claims.source: Geometry (lateral area of a conical frustum); simpler area approximations in use: Deniz Sungur D et al., Restor Dent Endod 2016;41(2):114-20 (PMID 27200279); Al-Haddad AY et al., Int J Biomater 2018:1731857 (PMID 30154852)

claims.claim: r 0.42 · R 0.45 mm, h 1.00 mm → A 2.73 mm², τ = 2.94 MPa (illustrative)
claims.source: Toy model / schematic: illustrative values, within reported GP + sealer ranges (Ungor M et al., Int Endod J 2006;39(8):643-7, PMID 16872459; Jainaen A et al., Int Endod J 2007;40(11):882-90, PMID 17877721; Al-Haddad AY et al., Int J Biomater 2018:1731857, PMID 30154852)

claims.claim: Mean shear stress to dislodge the filling: adhesion + friction + interlock
claims.source: Collares FM et al., Int Endod J 2016;49(9):836-49 (PMID 26331627); Goracci C et al., J Endod 2005;31(8):608-12 (PMID 16044046); Gesi A et al., J Endod 2005;31(11):809-13 (PMID 16249724); interlock (tubule penetration as micromechanical lock): Deniz Sungur D et al., Restor Dent Endod 2016;41(2):114-20 (PMID 27200279)

claims.claim: A lab number: compare within a study, not across studies; slice thickness, root third, core, plunger size, load speed, storage and area formula all shift the MPa
claims.source: Brichko J et al., J Endod 2018;44(8):1237-45 (PMID 29935874); Collares FM et al., Int Endod J 2016;49(9):836-49 (PMID 26331627); Pane ES et al., J Endod 2013;39(5):669-73 (PMID 23611388)

claims.claim: Clinical relevance: unproven; lab link to seal mixed; none to outcomes
claims.source: Lab evidence conflicts: no correlation between push-out and fluid transport, Moinzadeh AT et al., Int Endod J 2015;48(2):193-8 (PMID 24749656, methacrylate sealer); strong correlation, Neelakantan P et al., Int Endod J 2011;44(6):491-8 (PMID 21255047, AH Plus). No clinical outcome study links push-out MPa to treatment outcome (absence of evidence)

caption:
What does a push-out MPa actually measure?

A 1 mm slice of filled root is pushed apical → coronal with a plunger narrower than the canal.
Peak force ÷ canal-wall area = the mean shear stress to dislodge the filling: adhesion + friction + interlock, not pure sealer–dentin bond.
Slice thickness, root third, core, plunger size and load speed all shift it, so compare within a study, not across studies. Lab links to seal are mixed, and no link to clinical outcomes has been shown.

Refs: Pane 2013, J Endod · Collares 2016, Int Endod J · Brichko 2018, J Endod · Neelakantan 2011, Int Endod J · Moinzadeh 2015, Int Endod J
